title: Consumption and treatment services motion deferred
subtitle: Affordable housing tax exemption changes, 2024 food safety report, and a sustainability award for 420 Kingscourt Drive.
overview: The Community and Health Services Committee spent most of its meeting on a motion about the Kitchener consumption and treatment services (CTS) site. The motion asked the Province to fund the site and to allow the Region to support it. After hearing delegations and staff, the committee voted to defer the motion to April 23, 2025 {{vote:m3}}. It asked for the relevant legislation and a legal opinion on Council's rights first.

The committee also recommended housekeeping changes to the Property Tax Exemption for Affordable Housing Program {{vote:m1}}. It also recommended asking the Province and the Canada Revenue Agency to let tenants in exempt housing keep the Ontario Energy and Property Tax Credit. Staff said the exemption defers tax revenue and is spread across the rest of the tax base.

The committee received the 2024 Food Safety Program Report for information. Staff said about 30 public health inspectors cannot reach every complaint or low-risk premise, so inspections are prioritized by risk. Some councillors suggested inspector capacity be considered in the next budget. The committee also recognized staff who won a Federation of Canadian Municipalities award for the net-zero 420 Kingscourt Drive housing build.

decisions.detail: The committee deferred the motion asking the Province to fund and permit the Kitchener CTS site to April 23, 2025, pending the legislation and a legal opinion {{vote:m3}}.

decisions.item: Affordable housing property tax exemption: housekeeping amendments
decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the housekeeping amendments to the Property Tax Exemption for Affordable Housing Program {{vote:m1}}.
The committee recommended asking the Province and the Canada Revenue Agency to let tenants in exempt affordable housing stay eligible for the Ontario Energy and Property Tax Credit.

debate: Delegations, including a drug action team, a health centre and people with lived experience, urged support for the motion. They said the site saved lives, eased pressure on emergency services and had broad local support. They described the request as a letter to the Province.

Staff said the Region does not fund health services, which are a provincial responsibility, and that taking on the cost would be over $1.2 million. They said such costs tend to stay with municipalities. They also said the Province has stated that Hub funding, about four times the CTS amount, would be withdrawn if organizations try to continue CTS operations.

Some councillors said they would not risk the HART Hub funding, with one saying they could not support the motion. Others supported it to speak out and to urge the Province to follow the court injunction. One councillor doubted the Province would respond to a letter and called for a broader drug strategy.

Staff said the legislation bars municipalities from supporting CTS without ministerial approval and that the minister appeared unlikely to grant it. A councillor said the committee needed the legislation and a legal opinion on Council's rights, which led to the deferral.

On the housing item, councillors asked what case-by-case condominium eligibility means. Staff said they want to check owners' motives and guard against renovictions. Staff said other municipalities had not succeeded in getting the tax credit rule changed, but they would help affected tenants find other supports.
